instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in a few changes of water until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 1 3/4 cups water, bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 18 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered while the potatoes braise.
Cut the potatoes into 1 to 1 1/2 inch chunks and rinse them under cold water to wash off the extra starch. Drain them well.
Mince the garlic. In a bowl, whisk the garlic with the soy sauce, mirin, sugar, rice syrup, pepper and 3/4 cup water.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes in a single layer and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, turning them when the bottoms sizzle, until crisp on the outside.
Pour in the sauce and bring it to a boil. Stir, cover, turn the heat to medium, and braise for 5 minutes, until a fork slides into the potatoes.
Turn the heat to medium-high, take the lid off, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the potatoes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
method_notes: Okonomi Kitchen pan-fries the potatoes first for a crisp outside, then braises them in a soy, mirin, sugar and syrup sauce and finishes uncovered until it clings. Beyond Kimchee skips the frying and simmers the potatoes in a soy and syrup sauce with a piece of kelp, and Aaron and Claire simmer in a thinner sauce for about 20 minutes. This follows Okonomi Kitchen, doubled for 4, with the dark soy sauce replaced by more regular soy sauce as that recipe allows, and rice added to make it a dinner. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 to 4 days and do not freeze well.
